likely_trigger: Before the open on Oct 16 Fox Factory announced that its CEO was stepping down with an interim CEO appointed the same day, reported preliminary Q3 results below its own guidance, and lowered its fiscal 2026 outlook.

trigger_source.title: Fox Factory Holding Corp. - Fox Factory Announces CEO Transition
trigger_source.publisher: Fox Factory Holding Corp. (GlobeNewswire press release; PubT copy on Bigdata.com)

trigger_quote: Independent Director Douglas Grimm Appointed Interim CEO; Board Initiates Search for Permanent CEO [...] Preliminary Third Quarter Fiscal 2026 Results Below Expectations; Updates Fiscal 2026 Outlook for Divestiture of Marucci and Operating Performance
tier_reason: Sudden CEO departure (stepping down and resigning from the Board effective Oct 15, interim CEO effective Oct 16) combined with preliminary results below guidance and a fiscal 2026 outlook cut; trigger-tiers lists 'Sudden CEO or CFO departure' as Tier A. The guidance cut alone would be Tier B unless the outlook was recently reaffirmed (a plaintiff firm asserts it was reaffirmed in May and raised in August - attributed, not verified).

alternatives.explanation: CEO departure plus preliminary Q3 miss and FY2026 outlook cut (single pre-market release)
alternatives.why: Released before the open (The Fly 12:20Z; MT Newswires 12:51Z: shares down >22% pre-market). Peers -0.2%; abnormal -12.8%, t -5.70; volume 4.78x average (script).

alternatives.explanation: Marucci Sports divestiture (closed Sept 25) reducing the outlook mechanically
alternatives.why: Company attributes ~$63M of the net-sales reduction to Marucci; the adjusted EBITDA cut ($176-196M to $140-150M) also reflects PVG supply disruption, input inflation and AAG upfit problems.
Script peer return -0.24%, XRT theme -0.9%, expected return -0.5%.

prior_statement_check.quote: To summarize, our cost programs are executing on plan and our balance sheet health is improving. We remain confident in our full year outlook with margin expansion weighted to the second half.

source.title: Fox Factory Holding Corp: Q2 2026 Earnings Call on Aug 6, 2026 - Transcript (Quartr)
source.location: Prepared remarks, financial outlook section closing (speaker hands back to 'Mike'; speaker name not shown in the chunk - likely CFO Dennis Schemm, to verify), chunk 26

prior_statement_check.note: Same passage gave Q3 guidance of net sales $355M-$380M and adjusted EBITDA $46M-$54M, and referred to 'the continued impact of chassis supply constraints' and a bike 'supplier disruption' - so supply issues were mentioned but described as normalizing. Plaintiff firm Levi & Korsinsky attributes to CFO Schemm on May 7, 2026: "We are reaffirming our full year guide for 2026." (attributed; primary transcript not opened). EDGAR full-text search "full year outlook" (CIK 1424929, 2024-10-16..2026-10-15) returned only the Q3 2025 earnings release (2025-11-06).

notes: trigger_public_at is the earliest timestamp seen for the results news (The Fly 2026-10-16T12:20:06Z = 08:20 ET); the GlobeNewswire release time itself was not retrieved. The 8-K was filed after the close (20:06 ET), so the press release, not the 8-K, reached the market first. 8-K: Board approved the CEO transition on Oct 15; Mr. Dennison remains employed pending a transition agreement; interim CEO Grimm joined the Board in March 2026 and served on the Audit Committee and the Transformation Committee. Plaintiff-firm investigation notices after day 0: Levi & Korsinsky (2026-10-16T23:18Z), Schall Brown & Schwartz (2026-10-18). Prior securities class action (Marselis, N.D. Ga. 1:24-cv-00747, class period 2021-2023, demand/inventory statements) was dismissed with prejudice on 2026-02-10 with no appeal.
